title: GPU memory safeguards: adaptive batching, KV eviction, and graceful OOM recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We are observing intermittent GPU OOMs in the serving fleet under high-concurrency workloads that use continuous batching and large KV caches. Root causes include underestimated per-request memory accounting (long prompt + long generation), uncontrolled batch growth from spikey arrival patterns, and KV cache retention of large prefix states for many active sessions. OOMs cause request failures, retries that amplify load, and in some cases node instability requiring reboots.

Goal: Implement multi-layered safeguards to prevent OOMs and to recover gracefully when memory pressure exceeds safe thresholds. Safeguards should: (1) estimate and reserve memory before admission, (2) throttle or shrink batches when headroom is low, (3) enforce KV cache memory budgets and eviction policies, (4) provide deterministic fallback paths (smaller model / zero-cache mode) with transparent retries and rate-limited circuit breaking, and (5) ship observability and alerting to measure effectiveness.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration tests that induce peak allocations show 0 OOM crashes in 72h sustained load for canary nodes
System reduces batch sizes or admission under memory pressure and keeps tail latency SLOs within agreed degradation budgets
KV cache enforces per-tenant and per-model memory budgets; eviction prevents sustained >90% GPU memory utilization
Fallback flow to model-compact variant or non-KV path succeeds with clear metrics and <5% error increase vs baseline
Dashboard with OOM count, memory headroom histogram, fallback rate, retry rate, and per-model per-node memory footprints is available and linked in alerts
design_notes: Key ideas: 1) Memory accounting layer that calculates an estimated GPU working set per request = model_base_ram + max(prompt_len * token_ram, kv_miss_extra) + generation_window * token_ram. Use conservative multipliers (1.2x) until we have better telemetry. 2) Admission controller: compact preflight that rejects or declines admission if estimated allocation + current_allocations > node_budget - reserved_buffer. 3) Dynamic batching policy: an exponential decay-based batch cap that tightens under high variance; when headroom < threshold, switch to single-shot or micro-batches. 4) KV cache eviction: tiered eviction combining LRU with token-length-aware heuristics and optional TTL for long-idle sessions. Provide a per-tenant soft quota and background compaction that evicts or compresses KV entries (quantize keys) when under pressure. 5) Fallback strategies: (a) fallback model family (quantized or smaller), (b) no-KV execution path (recompute prefixes), (c) reduce max_new_tokens. 6) Retry semantics: idempotent retries with jittered backoff and a retry budget counter per request to avoid retry storms. 7) Circuit breaker: node-level and cluster-level breakers triggered by sustained high OOM-like memory pressure metrics. 8) Telemetry and traces: sample memory maps, peak allocation per request, KV eviction events, batch size evolution, and fallback triggers.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2w): add conservative memory estimator and admission hook in runtime (PR-#1). Phase 2 (2w): implement batch-size controller with headroom feedback loop and integrate with serving scheduler (PR-#2). Phase 3 (3w): KV budget enforcement and eviction daemon; add per-tenant quotas and compaction paths (PR-#3). Phase 4 (2w): implement fallback model routing + retry budget; integrate with router for automatic model substitution (PR-#4). Phase 5 (1w): dashboards, alerts, and synthetic load tests. Keep each phase behind feature flags and gated canary rollout.

Important implementation notes: prefer minimal changes to the hot path; the admission check must be O(1) and use shared atomic counters for current_allocations. Batch controller runs in the scheduler event loop; KV eviction runs in a low-priority background worker to avoid interfering with serving critical paths.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dev cluster canary (2 nodes) with flag runtime.memory_guard=on for a week, run chaos tests. 2) Gradual production canary: 1% of traffic for 48h, then 10% for 72h, monitoring memory headroom and fallback rate. 3) If metrics stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over one week. 4) Quick rollback path: kill flag or routing to rollback image; emergency rollback script documented in runbook. 5) Release notes and customer-facing postmortem template prepared if we see increased fallback rates affecting SLAs.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests around estimator math and edge cases (extreme prompt lengths).
- Integration tests: synthetic workloads with scripted arrival patterns to verify batch shrink/growth and admission decisions.
- Chaos tests: simulate memory spike, artificially inflate KV size and assert evictions and fallback triggers.
- Load tests: end-to-end with real models (small/medium/large) to measure tail latency and throughput under active guard.
- Regression tests to ensure no increase in error rates for P0 tenants.
- Post-deploy synthetic canary that attempts to force OOM path; system must either prevent OOM or execute fallback path reliably.
risks: False positives from conservative estimator may reduce throughput and increase cost
Fallback to smaller models degrades output quality; need acceptance criteria for quality regressions
Background eviction could affect latency if it competes for CPU/GPU resources (mitigate via low priority workers)
Complexity in admission control could interact with autoscaling and lead to underutilization if not tuned
notes_comments: 2026-03-02: Architecture sync — decided on conservative estimator multiplier 1.2x until empirical correction is implemented. (Aisha)

2026-03-05: Design review — frontend SDK teams concerned about transparent fallback; agreed to add response metadata that indicates fallback path used so callers can handle degraded output. (Marco, Priya, Elena)

2026-03-09: Infra raised that eviction must respect encryption keys and KMS constraints for customers with private deployments — KV compaction only allowed if not affecting raw encrypted entries. Need legal/crypto consult. (Sam)
2026-03-11: Performance experiment: reducing reserved_buffer from 10% to 7% increased throughput but caused one canary OOM; reverted to 10% buffer. More telemetry required. (Marco)
